children: By Rob Curran
U.S. stocks fell as renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran near the Strait of Hormuz caused oil prices and long-term Treasury yields to rise.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 374.09 points, or 0.70%, to 53185.90. The S&P 500 lost 25.62 points, or 0.33%, to 7686.14, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite declined 31.53 points, or 0.12%, to 26370.89.
Oil futures rose $2.36 or 2.8%, to $85.76 a barrel. The U.S. struck Iranian rocket launchers which it said were preparing to mine the contested strait. Iran struck back at a U.S. base in Jordan.

The yield on the policy-sensitive two-year Treasury was unchanged. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note rose 0.036 percentage point to 4.757%. The 30-year bond yield gained 0.041 percentage point to 5.248.

Recently, long-term Treasury yields have tracked oil prices, a critical factor in inflation trends. Higher yields are likely to cause further increases in mortgage and loan rates. Speaking on CNBC, Goldman Sachs Chief Executive David Solomon said the recent surge in long-term Treasury rates bore watching but was not yet an urgent matter.
The U.S. dollar slipped against rivals as traders weighed the outlook for Federal Reserve action.

High-momentum artificial-intelligence bets including chip makers and mega-cap tech stocks have stalled following a stellar earnings season. One strategist said they would remain under pressure until the next earnings season.

"It's becoming a 'show-me' market in that space because things have gone up so much," said J.D. Joyce, president of Houston financial advisory Joyce Wealth Management. The "no-man's land" between earnings seasons could be rocky for these stocks, the strategist warned.
"Are people going to hold on while they wait or is there going to be a new narrative while we're waiting?" Joyce said.

Nvidia shares rose 1.4% to $220.50 after the AI chip maker said it plans to invest $3.5 billion in chip designer MediaTek, deepening their collaboration to build next-generation AI computing platforms.

Amazon declined 2.5%, the most in more than a month, to $259.77 after the Federal Trade Commission reportedly prepared to file a lawsuit alleging it had manipulated prices businesses paid to advertise on its retail platform, reaping tens of billions of dollars in deceptive fees during a seven-year period.
Deal activity intensified as investment bankers worked the weekend ahead of another "merger Monday."
Aon agreed to buy rival insurance brokerage USI Insurance from investment firm KKR for roughly $17 billion, including debt.

Oil-services giant SLB agreed to acquire thermal management company Kelvion from an investment consortium including Apollo Global Management for $4.1 billion. Kelvion is a major provider of critical cooling services for data centers.
Eli Lilly agreed to buy biotech firm Merida Biosciences for up to $2.875 billion in cash, seeking to bulk up its immunology portfolio.

Shares of West Coast utilities fell after the California State Assembly removed a provision for utilities' liability protection from a wildfire bill. PG&E tumbled 20% to $13.27. Edison International fell 23% to $53.98. Sempra declined 3.1% to $81.70.
The rebound in oil prices weighed on cruise lines and other fuel-price sensitive companies.
Gold futures fell $47, or 1.1%, to $4431.10 a troy ounce, trimming year-to-date gains to 2.4%.
Write to Rob Curran at rob.curran@wsj.com
